description.value: A cue-reactivity fMRI study examining neural correlates of adherence to extended-release naltrexone pharmacotherapy in fully detoxified heroin-dependent individuals.

spans.text: we utilized blood oxygenation level-dependent functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in conjunction with a validated cue-induced craving procedure to examine neural correlates of XRNTX adherence.

value: we hypothesized that pre-treatment mPFC response to heroin-related stimuli will predict the number of XRNTX injections accepted by the participants.

spans.text: Inclusion criteria were: (1) 18–55 years of age; (2) DSM-IV-TR diagnosis of opioid dependence; (3) active opioid use, confirmed by urine toxicology screen and self-reported monthly intravenous heroin use for more than 2 weeks in the past 3 months; (4) urine toxicology screen negative for opioids after detoxification; (5) good physical health as determined by history and physical examination, by screening blood work-up and by urinalysis.

spans.text: Exclusion criteria were: (1) current chronic medical illnesses; (2) current use of potentially confounding medications such as anti-dopaminergic agents, anti-depressants, anticonvulsants, mood stabilizers and beta-blockers; (3) current DSM-IV-TR Axis I psychiatric disorders with the exception of opioid and nicotine dependence, non-dependent cocaine abuse and depressive disorders; (4) lifetime history of concurrent intravenous cocaine and heroin (speedball) administration; (5) pregnancy or breastfeeding; (6) history of clinically significant head trauma
